events.title: Proposed ruling: refund_partial $1.13 (model confidence 0.82)
events.body:
This is a RydeTAXI trip, so the metered fare moves with distance and any unexplained extra kilometre enters the fare [F1][F6][RD-1][RD-2]. The data layer finds one off-route segment, 22:57–23:01, 2.19 km driven versus 1.38 km on the optimal route, adding 0.80 km and reaching 1014 m from the optimal route [F3]. No exemption applies to it.

RD-4 requires a traffic incident on the replaced stretch of the optimal route, reported before the detour and still open during the window; the trace records no qualifying incident, and speed band alone does not exempt [F10][F11][F12][F13][RD-4]. The driver's statement that Ayer Rajah Expressway "was crawling" [F9] is a statement, not a system record, and RD-4 gives no independent exempting force to a traffic band. RD-3 does not apply because the rider named no stop or destination change and the chat contains only pickup logistics [F7][F8][RD-3]. RD-5 fails because the driver never proposed a route before leaving the optimal route — the only chats are at 22:45 and 22:46 about the pickup point, both before the segment, with no route request and no agreement, and the driver's explanation came only after the fact [F7][F8][F9][RD-5].

Amount: the segment is a non-exempt detour, so the rider recovers its extra kilometres at the trip's per-km rate, $17.50 ÷ 12.4 km = $1.4113/km; 0.80 km × $1.4113/km = $1.1290, rounded to $1.13 [F3][F6][RD-2]. The headline excess distance billed is $2.33 (1.6 km × $1.41/km), which exceeds the segment amount because it includes the map-matching residual on the rest of the trip; RD-2 refunds only the non-exempt segment's extra km and does not refund that residual [F1][F4][RD-2]. Neither advocate's requested outcome survives: the rider's request for full refund of the extra distance is not supported because only 0.80 km is a non-exempt detour, and the driver's request for no action fails because the deviation is unexplained [F3][F9][RD-1][RD-2].

Driver's profile shows route_disputes_upheld_90d = 0, so this case does not make the breach "repeated" and no account flag is added [F16][RD-6].

events.title: Notices sent to rider and driver
events.body:
RIDER: Your fare dispute is decided in your favour in part. On your RydeTAXI trip, one stretch of the route went off course: about 0.80 km further than the best route for that stretch, with no good reason on record for it. That extra distance is refunded at the trip's per-km rate, giving you $1.13. It is paid as a Ryde voucher, not cash or card. The rest of your extra-distance request is not refunded, as only that stretch counts as an unexplained detour. No change is made to your account.

DRIVER: The fare dispute on this trip is decided partly against you. Records show one stretch where you drove about 0.80 km further than the best route, and nothing on record explains it: no reported incident on the road you avoided, and no route agreed with the rider beforehand. You keep the rest of the fare. $1.13 is paid to the rider as a Ryde voucher, not taken as cash from you. Your account is not flagged or restricted; this is not treated as a repeated breach. Keep offering route changes in chat before deviating.
